# Cinema Teatro Sestito Website

This repository contains the website of Cinema Teatro Sestito, built with R, blogdown, and Hugo.

## Project Documentation

Project status, decisions, and open tasks are documented in:

- `docs/project-status.md`

The documentation index and guides are in `docs/README.md`. Documentation for
the historical programming scripts is available in:

- `docs/guides/historical-programming.md`

Always consult these files before proposing structural changes.

## Important Rules

### Never modify generated files

Do not edit files inside the `public/` directory.

The `public/` folder is automatically generated by Hugo and its contents will be overwritten during site builds.

### Content Structure

- Content pages and articles are located in `content/`
- Templates and layouts are located in `layouts/`
- Static assets are located in `static/`
- R scripts are located in `R/`

### Historical Programming Pages

The historical programming pages:

- years
- sources
- genres
- countries

and their related index charts are automatically generated by R scripts located in `R/`.

To change these pages:

1. Update the source data in `static/data/`
2. Modify the generation scripts in `R/` if necessary
3. Do not manually edit generated pages

### Writing Guidelines

When creating or revising articles, film entries, and historical content:

- Write in Italian.
- Use a welcoming, clear, and professional tone.
- Maintain historical accuracy.
- Prefer concise and readable prose.
- Preserve existing metadata and front matter.
- Respect the site's established style and terminology.

### Development Guidelines

Before modifying code:

1. Determine whether a page is manually written or automatically generated.
2. Check whether the requested change belongs in:
   - data (`static/data/`)
   - R scripts (`R/`)
   - content (`content/`)
   - templates (`layouts/`)
3. Prefer fixing generation logic instead of manually editing generated output.

### Hugo and blogdown

This site uses Hugo through blogdown.

When proposing changes:

- Follow Hugo conventions.
- Preserve existing front matter structures.
- Avoid introducing dependencies unless clearly justified.
- Keep templates modular and maintainable.

## Generated Historical Archive Content

Many archive pages are generated automatically from cinema programming datasets.

Before editing a page, determine whether it is:

- manually authored content
- generated content

For generated content:

- identify the originating R script
- identify the source dataset
- modify the generation process rather than the generated file

Prefer reproducible changes over manual corrections.

When generating R code:

- use tidyverse conventions when appropriate
- preserve existing project naming conventions
- generate clean Markdown compatible with Hugo and blogdown
- avoid hard-coded paths

## Hugo Build and Temporary File Policy

This repository is built with Hugo through blogdown.

To avoid excessive disk usage:

- Never create duplicate Hugo sites.
- Never create backup copies of the entire repository.
- Never create temporary project folders outside the repository.
- Never generate additional `public-*`, `site-*`, `build-*`, `tmp-*`, or `test-*` directories.
- Always reuse the existing project structure.

When testing changes:

- Use the existing Hugo development server.
- Regenerate content only when necessary.
- Replace generated output rather than creating parallel copies.

### Generated Directories

The following directories may be regenerated automatically:

- `public/`
- `resources/`

Do not create alternative versions of these folders.

### File Generation Rules

When generating code or content:

- Write directly to the intended destination file.
- Update existing files when appropriate.
- Avoid creating numbered versions such as:

  - `index-new.md`
  - `index-final.md`
  - `index-final-v2.md`
  - `layout-copy.html`

unless explicitly requested.

### blogdown and Hugo

Prefer workflows that modify source files only:

- `content/`
- `layouts/`
- `static/`
- `assets/`
- `R/`

Avoid actions that trigger unnecessary full-site rebuilds.

## Repository Hygiene

This project has previously experienced storage growth caused by:

- repeated Hugo builds
- duplicated generated sites
- temporary Copilot workspaces
- archived copies of generated content

Before creating new files, check whether an existing file can be updated instead.

Minimize file duplication and keep generated artefacts to the minimum required.

## Build Output Policy

This project uses a single Hugo build output directory:

- public/

When building the site:

- Always use the existing public/ directory.
- Replace or update the existing build.
- Never create additional build directories.
- Never create temporary Hugo sites.
- Never create backup copies of generated websites.
- Never create folders such as:

  - public-copy/
  - public-new/
  - public-backup/
  - build/
  - build-test/
  - site-preview/
  - tmp-site/
  - temp-site/

If a build is required, regenerate the existing public/ folder instead of creating a parallel build.

The source of truth is:

- content/
- layouts/
- static/
- assets/
- R/

Generated output should exist only in public/.

## Agent Workspace Rules

Before creating a new folder, check whether an existing folder can be reused.

Prefer:
- updating existing files
- overwriting generated output
- reusing existing build artifacts

Avoid creating temporary workspaces, cloned repositories, or duplicate project trees unless explicitly requested.

## Repository Modification Rules

Work directly inside the current repository.

Do not create:
- temporary repositories
- cloned repositories
- copied project trees
- backup projects

All modifications must occur within the existing project directory.

## Documentation Governance

### README Policy

Keep `README.md` concise and focused on:

- project purpose
- setup instructions
- build instructions
- links to documentation

Do not place detailed technical documentation, implementation notes, design decisions, development history, or project planning information in `README.md`.

### Documentation Location

Detailed documentation belongs in the `docs/` directory.

Examples include:

- project status
- development decisions
- workflow documentation
- architecture documentation
- content generation processes
- Hugo customization notes
- R script documentation
- maintenance procedures
- data source documentation

When additional documentation is needed, create or update files in `docs/` instead of expanding `README.md`.

## Documentation Maintenance

Documentation is considered part of every change.

After making modifications:

1. Determine whether the change affects project documentation.
2. Update the relevant files in `docs/`.
3. Keep documentation synchronized with the current implementation.
4. Record important design decisions and workflow changes.
5. Remove outdated documentation when it no longer reflects the codebase.

Changes that require documentation review include:

- new R scripts
- changed generation workflows
- new Hugo templates
- architectural changes
- data structure changes
- build process changes
- content generation logic changes
- new dependencies

When documentation is modified:

- keep files organized by topic
- avoid duplication between documentation files
- place technical details in `docs/`
- keep `README.md` minimal

### Documentation Index

Maintain a clear structure inside `docs/`.

When creating new documentation:

- use descriptive filenames
- group related documentation together
- update any documentation index or cross-references
- avoid creating duplicate documentation files

Before creating a new documentation file, check whether an existing document should be updated instead.

## End-of-Task Checklist

Before completing any task:

- verify that generated content was not edited manually
- verify that changes were made in the correct source location
- verify that no duplicate files were created
- verify that no temporary build directories were created
- verify whether documentation in `docs/` should be updated
- keep `README.md` concise
